action_criteria.expected_evidence: Serum anti-GluN1 positive (1:32); sodium 131 mmol/L; thyroid function, thyroid antibodies, neuronal-surface and onconeural antibodies normal or negative; beta-hCG negative
action_criteria.label: Obtain the serum work-up (blood count, chemistry, thyroid function and antibodies, HIV, beta-hCG, serum anti-GluN1 cell-based assay read with the CSF)
action_criteria.rationale: Screens metabolic, toxic, infectious and thyroid causes of catatonia and gives the serum anti-GluN1 result, which supports but cannot replace the CSF assay.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Normal MRI: no signal abnormality, restricted diffusion or enhancement; normal hippocampi
action_criteria.label: Obtain contrast-enhanced brain MRI to exclude HSV encephalitis, structural lesions and overlapping demyelination; a normal MRI does not exclude anti-NMDAR encephalitis
action_criteria.rationale: Excludes HSV encephalitis and structural causes of catatonia before LP; it is normal in most patients and does not confirm the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: No pleocytosis, no oligoclonal bands, normal IgG index, HSV PCR negative, CSF anti-GluN1 IgG positive (1:16)
action_criteria.label: Analyze CSF for cells, protein and glucose, OCB/IgG index, HSV PCR and a cell-based IgG anti-GluN1 assay interpreted in parallel with serum
action_criteria.rationale: With a normal MRI and a bland CSF, the CSF cell-based anti-GluN1 assay is the test that establishes the diagnosis.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Moderate generalized slowing with FIRDA; no epileptiform discharges or extreme delta brush on the routine study
action_criteria.label: Obtain EEG for encephalopathic and epileptiform abnormalities, explicitly assessing for extreme delta brush
action_criteria.rationale: An encephalopathic EEG separates an organic catatonia from a primary psychiatric one; non-convulsive seizures must also be excluded.

action_criteria.label: Perform pelvic and abdominal ultrasound to screen for an ovarian teratoma
action_criteria.rationale: Young women carry the highest teratoma risk; tumor removal would be part of first-line treatment.

action_criteria.expected_evidence: Seizure burden and evolution of the background over 24 hours or more
action_criteria.label: Escalate to continuous EEG monitoring to quantify seizure burden and detect non-convulsive seizures
action_criteria.rationale: Catatonic unresponsiveness with lip-smacking and facial twitching cannot be separated clinically from non-convulsive seizures.

prohibited_recommendations: Do not give haloperidol or other high-potency D2 antagonists for agitation: patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis are prone to severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic-malignant-like reactions.
Do not delay immunotherapy while waiting for the anti-NMDAR antibody result when clinical probability is high: antibody turnaround can take 1 to 2 weeks and delay worsens outcome.
Do not attribute the presentation to a primary psychiatric disorder while seizures, dyskinesias, autonomic instability, an abnormal EEG or CSF inflammation remain unexplained.
Do not perform lumbar puncture without prior imaging in a patient with altered consciousness, focal signs, or new seizures: exclude mass effect first.
Do not interpret a negative serum anti-NMDAR antibody as ruling out the disease; the CSF assay is the gold standard and may be positive when serum is negative.
required_recommendations: Start IV acyclovir 10 mg/kg every 8 hours at presentation, and stop it once CSF HSV PCR is negative and the antibody diagnosis is established; repeat the PCR on a second CSF sample if the first LP was within 72 hours of onset and HSV encephalitis remains plausible.

Start first-line immunotherapy without waiting for the antibody result once infection is reasonably excluded: IV methylprednisolone 1 g daily for 5 days with IVIG 0.4 g/kg/day for 5 days (2 g/kg total) or plasma exchange (5 to 7 exchanges).

Pelvic ultrasound shows no tumor: repeat pelvic imaging (MRI or transvaginal ultrasound) if the response to immunotherapy is poor or the disease relapses, and continue tumor surveillance during follow-up.
Treat seizures with an antiseizure medication such as levetiracetam or lacosamide; avoid valproate in a woman able to become pregnant; seizures respond mainly to immunotherapy.
Monitor with continuous EEG for non-convulsive seizures while consciousness fluctuates or seizures persist.
Admit to the ICU / neurocritical care for catatonia with refusal of food, agitation and the need for continuous EEG, with airway assessment and cardiac monitoring.

If there is no meaningful clinical improvement 10 to 14 days after first-line therapy, escalate to rituximab (375 mg/m² weekly for 4 doses or 1 g twice 2 weeks apart, after hepatitis B screening) and/or cyclophosphamide; discuss fertility preservation before cyclophosphamide.
Treat agitation, insomnia and catatonia with benzodiazepines (lorazepam) first.
While catatonia prevents oral intake, give IV fluids, monitor intake, weight and electrolytes, consider nasogastric feeding, and give venous thromboembolism prophylaxis for immobility.
Neurology-led care with psychiatry for behavioral management.

avoided_actions.rationale: Transthoracic echo is not indicated for anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it adds cost without informing diagnosis or management unless a discrete cardiac concern (e.g., new murmur, embolic stroke) coexists.
EMG/NCS plays no role in the diagnostic workup of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it neither confirms the antibody-mediated CNS process nor distinguishes among the differential diagnoses.
Amyloid PET targets Alzheimer pathology and contributes no information to the diagnosis or treatment of autoimmune encephalitis in a young patient with subacute neuropsychiatric symptoms.

DaTscan evaluates nigrostriatal dopaminergic function and has no role in autoimmune encephalitis; the orofacial dyskinesias of anti-NMDAR encephalitis are antibody-mediated, not presynaptic dopaminergic.

differential.key_features: Afebrile; CSF HSV PCR negative without pleocytosis; normal MRI without temporal signal, hemorrhage or restricted diffusion; CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Other antibody-mediated encephalitis (anti-LGI1, CASPR2, GABA-B, AMPA)

differential.diagnosis: Primary psychiatric disorder (catatonia / first-episode psychosis / adjustment disorder)
differential.key_features: Orofacial dyskinesias and facial twitching, variable rigidity, generalized EEG slowing with FIRDA, right temporal electrographic seizures on continuous EEG and CSF anti-GluN1 positive.

differential.diagnosis: Drug-induced psychosis or neuroleptic malignant syndrome
differential.key_features: No medications and no antipsychotic exposure; urine drug screen and ethanol negative; temperature 37.4 °C and CK 164 U/L.

key_clinical_evidence: Ten days of insomnia, then paranoid delusions, mutism with waxy flexibility alternating with agitation, refusal to eat, orofacial dyskinesias and variable rigidity four weeks after a flu-like illness; continuous EEG adds seizures: four of the six Graus 2016 groups (behavior, speech, movement disorder, seizures).
CSF IgG anti-GluN1 positive (titer 1:16) on cell-based assay: definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis (Graus 2016), with an otherwise bland CSF; serum positive 1:32 is read with the CSF.
MRI is normal; MRI is normal or non-specific in about two thirds and excludes HSV encephalitis and structural causes.

Routine EEG shows generalized slowing with FIRDA and no extreme delta brush; continuous EEG captures three subclinical right temporal seizures; extreme delta brush, when present, supports but does not establish the diagnosis.
Pelvic ultrasound shows no tumor: repeat pelvic imaging if the response to immunotherapy is poor or the disease relapses.
Earlier immunotherapy is associated with better outcome (Titulaer 2013); benzodiazepines, not antipsychotics, are first-line for the catatonia (Lejuste 2016).

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: A viral-like prodrome precedes about 70% of anti-NMDAR encephalitis; it does not establish viral encephalitis, which CSF PCR addresses.
red_herrings.data_point: Flu-like illness with sore throat and low-grade fever four weeks before the neuropsychiatric syndrome.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Suggests a primary viral encephalitis (HSV) or post-viral psychosis; tempts the agent to commit to empiric antiviral therapy without pursuing autoimmune workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Catatonia with orofacial dyskinesias, variable rigidity and an abnormal EEG are red flags that mandate exclusion of anti-NMDAR encephalitis before accepting a psychiatric diagnosis.
red_herrings.data_point: Acute psychiatric presentation (insomnia, poisoning delusions, bizarre behavior) in a previously well young adult, already diagnosed with adjustment disorder by the university clinic.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Anchors the agent on a primary psychiatric diagnosis (first-episode psychosis, brief psychotic disorder) and delays neurologic workup.

red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Hyponatremia occurs in anti-NMDAR encephalitis but is more typical of anti-LGI1 encephalitis; it needs its own work-up and correction and does not point away from the diagnosis.
red_herrings.intended_effect: Tempts the agent toward a primary metabolic-encephalopathy framing (SIADH from another cause, dehydration, polydipsia) instead of recognizing SIADH as a known complication of NMDAR-E.

contraindications: Class warning: haloperidol and other high-potency dopamine D2 antagonists are associated with severe extrapyramidal and neuroleptic malignant-like reactions in anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis.
Valproate: avoid in women able to become pregnant unless other options fail.
interactions: No current medications: no drug-drug interaction with the proposed acute agents.
Lorazepam IV: respiratory depression and sedation, additive with other sedatives; monitor respiration during dose titration for catatonia.
Acyclovir IV: crystal nephropathy risk, higher with poor oral intake; maintain IV hydration and monitor creatinine.
IVIG: risk of renal impairment and thrombosis; ensure hydration and avoid rapid infusion rates.
High-dose methylprednisolone: hyperglycemia, hypertension and hypokalemia; monitor glucose and electrolytes.
Levetiracetam: no clinically relevant pharmacokinetic interactions; renally cleared.
general.summary: No current medications. Class cautions for lorazepam, acyclovir, IVIG, high-dose corticosteroids, valproate and D2 antagonists listed above.
warnings: Rituximab: screen for hepatitis B (HBsAg, anti-HBc) before the first dose.
Cyclophosphamide is gonadotoxic and teratogenic: discuss fertility preservation and contraception.

results.finding: Definite anti-NMDAR encephalitis requires one or more of six major symptom groups and IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies, with CSF testing included; probable disease requires four groups (or three with a teratoma) of rapid onset plus an abnormal EEG or CSF pleocytosis or oligoclonal bands.
results.source: Graus F et al. Lancet Neurol 2016;15:391-404

results.finding: All patients had antibodies in CSF, whereas about 14% were negative in serum; CSF titers related more closely to outcome than serum titers.
results.source: Gresa-Arribas N et al. Lancet Neurol 2014;13:167-177

results.finding: 38% had a tumor, mostly ovarian teratoma; 53% improved within 4 weeks of first-line immunotherapy or tumor removal; second-line rituximab or cyclophosphamide after first-line failure was associated with better outcome; 81% had mRS 0-2 at 24 months.
results.source: Titulaer MJ et al. Lancet Neurol 2013;12:157-165

results.finding: Severe intolerance to antipsychotics (rigidity, hyperthermia, rhabdomyolysis, neuroleptic malignant-like reactions) was frequent in patients with anti-NMDAR encephalitis exposed to them.
results.source: Lejuste F et al. Neurol Neuroimmunol Neuroinflamm 2016;3:e280

anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis diagnosi.summary: Published criteria and cohort data on anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis: definite diagnosis rests on CSF IgG anti-GluN1 antibodies; first-line immunotherapy and tumor removal are followed by second-line agents when there is no response.

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: 19-year-old presenting as catatonic psychosis: no clinical seizures, normal MRI, near-normal CSF; subclinical seizures only on continuous EEG. Classic diagnostic puzzle with psychiatric masquerade.

patient.history_present_illness: A 19-year-old previously healthy right-handed woman of Asian descent was brought to the emergency department by her university dormitory resident advisor after 8 days of progressive and alarming behavioral changes. The patient had been seen by the university health clinic three days prior and diagnosed with adjustment disorder and given a referral for counseling, but her condition has worsened substantially since then. Her roommate reports that approximately 10 days ago the patient developed insomnia, staying up through the night and sending 'strange' text messages to family members that made no sense. Over the following days she became progressively more withdrawn, refused to eat, and began making accusations that her dormitory neighbors were trying to poison her food. On the day of presentation, the patient was found crouching in the corner of her room, trembling, and when the RA tried to speak with her, she became agitated and attempted to bite the RA. This represents a complete departure from her premorbid personality; she was described as quiet, studious, and reserved. Her parents have flown in from overseas and confirm she had no prior psychiatric history. They mention she had a 'flu-like illness' with sore throat and low-grade fever about four weeks ago lasting approximately five days that resolved without medical attention. She has no history of autoimmune disease, no substance use, and no prior hospitalizations. On arrival to the ED, the patient is alternating between agitation and what appears to be a catatonic unresponsiveness.

neurological_exam.additional: No nuchal rigidity on assessment. Temperature 37.4. No rash. Mild tachycardia present. Intermittent grimacing without clear precipitant.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils 4mm bilaterally, reactive to light. Doll's eye reflex intact. No clear nystagmus during examination. Intermittent lip-smacking and subtle facial twitching observed.
neurological_exam.gait: Ambulation observed briefly in room — erratic, no clear ataxia.
neurological_exam.mental_status: Alternates between agitated and catatonic states. During agitated phase: yelling, unable to follow commands, attempts to climb off stretcher. During catatonic phase: mute, staring, waxy flexibility of limbs. Orientation cannot be assessed. No consistent eye contact.
neurological_exam.motor: Tone variable — periods of rigidity alternating with normal tone. No focal weakness elicited. During brief cooperative windows: strength 5/5 upper extremities.
neurological_exam.reflexes: Biceps and patellar 2+ bilaterally. Plantar responses flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.sensory: Cannot be assessed due to limited cooperation.
